newsitem.title: FRANCE: Text of speech by French Socialist leader Jospin.
newsitem.headline: Text of speech by French Socialist leader Jospin.

text.p: Following is a partial text of a speech by Socialist leader Lionel Jospin on Sunday after projections showed the combined left leading the centre-right coalition in the first round of France's parliamentary election.

"We all feel the importance of this moment which comes after a too brief campaign, which maybe was not designed for the French to commit themselves, and at the same time after an intense campaign in which the French expressed themselves at least in this first round with great strength.

"...The proposals which the Socialists put to the country have been listened to. Our growth compared to 1993 and even to 1995 is very strong. More widely, the votes for the Socialists but also for the Radical Socialists and the Communist candidates, the representatives of the Greens and of the Citizens Movement, have strongly progressed compared to the last election. It is important that these forces unite and wage a positive second-round campaign based on proposals which centre on respect for the French.

"This important progression of the forces of the left and the ecologists seems to show that the French would like to see a left-wing future, not only because it is the left, not only because it is the real guardian of humanist values but also because it is the only one which shows itself ready to give itself the means to apply a strong policy on the most difficult problems with which France is confronted -- unemployment, inequalities, insecurity, housing, the problems of the future of children in education and training.

"What would a society which is not turned towards its future become? It would be an exhausted society, resigned and threatened by extremists. In the campaign for the first round the right did its best to twist our proposals and sometimes, in a contradictory way, to borrow them from us.

"The voters in the first round do not appear to have appeciated the excessively negative character of the campaign. The RPR and the UDF scored their weakest results in a long time. Neither their record, which is bad, nor their proposals, which were not defended, brought them the votes of many French people.

"The National Front has a high score, a score which is too high. All republican parties must question themselves to find out why this is so. The next government in any case must tackle as a priority the concerns of these French people, who are worried and who believe themselves forgotten and threatened, so as to answer their expectations.

"I call on all those who want a more balanced government and a new policy for France to unite in this second round. All those who aspire to change must unite because a change of majority is possible and desirable.

"I propose to all our citizens to commit themselves anew in political life, I propose to them a pact for change for a new democracy, which is honest and respectful towards everyone, with an ear for all, for a policy change -- a more audacious economic policy watchful of public spending, a more humane policy on social issues, a policy which will restart Frence, not for some but for all."
